incident-bot: PAGER: runtime-gpu-pool-3: recurring CUDA OOMs + high fragmentation signals. Error rate jump to ~22% across model-worker group between 22:11-22:18 UTC. Please ACK and triage.

oncall-kate: ACK. I'm taking lead. Notifying SRE + runtime-engineering. Any recent infra changes?

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-28T22:12Z: model:v3.0.1 canary -> 5% traffic, runtime config updated: token_buffer_pool=auto.

Ravi Desai: Support reported two customers seeing 500s: shoply (cart/checkout) and ledgerly (batch embeddings). CS has pages open.

Nora Liu: Looking at NVML samples now. GPUs show high used memory but also high "reserved" fraction. Several python workers exhibit large RSS and repeated small allocations.

SRE-runner: Attaching quick snapshot: ```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.free,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv
0, A100-80GB, 1 MiB, 81919 MiB, 98 %
1, A100-80GB, 512 MiB, 81408 MiB, 95 %
2, A100-80GB, 1024 MiB, 80960 MiB, 92 %
```

Ravi Desai: Telemetry shows KV cache per-session entries rising steadily for a subset of /chat/stateful calls. Evictions not keeping pace for long-lived sessions.

oncall-kate: Hypothesis 1: v3.0.1 introduced larger token buffer allocations for the new attention cache, which combined with stale KV entries causes fragmentation. Hypothesis 2: memory pool config change (`token_buffer_pool=auto`) allowed variable-sized allocs increasing fragmentation.

Nora Liu: Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) disable KV cache for canary traffic, 2) set token_buffer_pool=fixed:128MB, 3) throttle canary to 0% if needed. Which one should we try first?

oncall-kate: Let's flip KV cache off for canary and pin token pool to fixed for worker-03..07. Do one change at a time, monitor. Also hold any further rollouts.

ops-bot: Applying config change to workers runtime-worker-03..07: KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false; TOKEN_BUFFER_POOL=fixed:128MB. Restarting workers sequentially.

SRE-runner: After restarting 03..05: OOM events on those nodes dropped immediately. Cluster OOM rate fell from ~14/min to ~2/min. Latency p95 increased ~120ms across some paths.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic automatically reduced to 0% at 22:25Z due to health checks failing after rollout.

Ravi Desai: Customers: shoply still seeing intermittent failures during the rollout window, CS notified and queued mitigation steps. Ledgerly reports retries succeed after 10s.

oncall-kate: Excellent. For the full RCA we need: jemalloc stats, per-process malloc hooks (if enabled), pmap snapshots, Python tracestacks, dmesg kernel logs, and NVML timed traces. Upload to /mnt/incident/1772234567/artifacts.tar.gz.

Nora Liu: Collected artifacts and pushed: /mnt/incident/1772234567/jemalloc.txt, /mnt/incident/1772234567/nvml-samples.csv, /mnt/incident/1772234567/pmap-snapshots/, /mnt/incident/1772234567/dmesg.log. Noted repeated kernel message: "gpu memory allocation failed: no space left" interleaved with worker restarts.

Ravi Desai: Reproducer: mixing long-lived sessions (100k tokens) with short bursts increases fragmentation rapidly in local sim. Repro command: ```
python tools/sim_traffic.py --model v3.0.1 --mix long:0.2,short:0.8 --concurrency 60 --duration 45m
```

Nora Liu: jemalloc profiles show many small allocations (<=256B) from JSON serialization codepath while token buffers allocate large contiguous pages. The allocator's arena behavior shows fragmentation with free extents interleaved by allocated large spans.

oncall-kate: Temporary follow-ups:
- Keep KV cache disabled for canary and hold v3.0.1 rollout
- Schedule targeted rolling restarts to pick up TOKEN_BUFFER_POOL change across all workers
- Run nightly heap-dump at 03:00 UTC and a jemalloc background dump at 04:30 UTC

SRE-runner: Creating follow-up ticket INF-2912 assigned to Nora + Ravi for deep allocator RCA and mitigation. Recommend exploring jemalloc background thread enablement or switching to a pooled allocator for token buffers.

customer-success: Notifying affected customers: draft message ready. Tracking SLA credits if incident meets threshold.

Nora Liu: Early RCA notes: root cause likely interplay of two changes: token_buffer_pool=auto (deployment tweak) + v3.0.1 larger attention cache. Combined effect: more variable-sized allocations and reduced contiguous free extents -> fragmentation -> allocations fail despite nominal free memory.

Ravi Desai: Agreed. Actionable engineering fixes: revert token_buffer_pool to fixed sizing, add defensive limit on per-session KV cache size, implement periodic allocator defrag or enable jemalloc background thread, and add a batch-size auto-controller to prevent mixing many large long-lived sessions with high concurrency.

oncall-kate: Handoff: @Lee Chen you're on for the next shift. Keep KV cache disabled for canary and monitor OOM alarm `oom.runtime.gpu_fragmentation` closely. Run heap-dump at 03:00 UTC. Full incident notes and timeline in /ops/incidents/1772234567-notes.md.

Lee Chen: ack. I'll take it. Will run the scheduled dumps and check jemalloc outputs.

SRE-runner: Status update at 23:40 UTC: incident marked "mitigated"—OOMs reduced to baseline after config rollback and pool pinning. Customers largely recovered; one remaining customer had a short retry window.

oncall-kate: Closing pager for now. We'll reconvene for postmortem next week. Thanks all for quick triage and coordinated mitigation. :teamwork:
